Auston Trusty Denied Another USA Goal Before Celtic Return

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:07
Instaread

Auston Trusty heads back towards Celtic duty with two full matches and two clean sheets behind him. He came close to bringing a second international goal home, too.

Share

Stay

After an emotional scoring return against Haiti at the weekend, the defender was back in the USA starting line-up for the second leg of their Nations League quarter-final.

Trusty completed the 90 minutes in a 2–0 victory in Cincinnati, sealing an 8–0 aggregate win, but there was a moment early in the second half when he must have thought he had scored again.

There is plenty more in our latest Celtic news and transfers coverage.

In the 50th minute, he met a Christian Pulisic corner with a header towards the far post. Haiti defender Martin Expérience cleared it, although US Soccer’s official report suggested the ball “appeared” to have crossed the line before he intervened.

Get Celtic This MorningThe Celtic news that matters, in your inbox every morning. Free.Sign up free

No goal was awarded. Pulisic and Julian Hall’s first-half finishes remained the difference between the sides.

The bigger positive for Celtic is Trusty getting another full match under his belt.

He had been away from football following the death of his father, Walt, before returning with a goal and dedicating his performance to his dad in Saturday’s 6–0 win.

That was a special moment for the American. Following it with another start gives him valuable playing time before returning to Glasgow.

Martin O’Neill now has another defensive option to assess ahead of St Mirren’s visit on Saturday.

Two matches against Haiti will not settle the debate over Celtic’s strongest centre-back pairing. They do, however, mean Trusty is returning having played 180 competitive minutes rather than facing his first game after a lengthy absence.

With a busy run of domestic and European fixtures coming, that could be big for Celtic.

Liam Scales has made important contributions in recent weeks, while Cameron Carter-Vickers remains another option at the heart of the defence. Trusty’s return gives O’Neill a decision to make as well as room to rotate.

After a difficult few weeks personally, it is good to see him playing again and contributing at both ends of the pitch.
